section_summary: This section contains file notes, telegrams, despatches, intelligence reports, and newspaper clippings about Japanese naval policy from 1933 to 1938. The documents focus on naval parity, treaty limits, fleet expansion, the defense of Japanese possessions, and a proposed southward advance. A translated Japanese Navy pamphlet urges public support for rearmament, while a Dutch naval analysis considers the defense of the Netherlands East Indies.

subfiles.title: File note on a naval propaganda exhibition at Osaka
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch about a naval propaganda exhibition at the Matsuzakaya department store.
subfiles.summary: Records an exhibition scheduled for January 9–27, 1935.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs routing note
subfiles.about: Recommends an article for reading.
subfiles.summary: Calls an unidentified article worth reading.

subfiles.title: A British analysis of Japan's real designs
subfiles.about: Reproduces an Economist argument about Japan's demand for naval parity and its consequences.
subfiles.summary: The article rejects security and prestige as sufficient explanations for Japan's parity demand and argues that further expansion in the western Pacific is its likely aim. It urges British and American cooperation with China and the Soviet Union to deter aggression.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese tonnage proposals
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum commenting on Japan's proposed tonnage basis and defensive naval forces.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Hornbeck's comments on a proposed 1937 tonnage baseline.

subfiles.title: File note on naval budget demands
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Japanese naval demands for the 1936–37 budget.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a despatch concerning Japanese naval budget demands.

subfiles.title: Newspaper excerpt on Navy budget demands
subfiles.about: Reports a dispute between Japanese finance and navy officials over proposed budget reductions.
subfiles.summary: Finance officials urged cuts; navy officials said their demands were the minimum consistent with national defense.

subfiles.title: File note on Army and Navy Department appointments
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch translating rules restricting senior Army and Navy Department posts to active officers.
subfiles.summary: Indexes amended appointment regulations and enclosed translations.

subfiles.title: File note on Navy organization investigation
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch about a proposed Navy Organization Investigation Council.
subfiles.summary: Indexes information on the proposed council.

subfiles.title: Excerpt on a proposed Navy Organization Investigation Council
subfiles.about: Describes a proposed council and the Navy's policy of home defense and southward advance.
subfiles.summary: The proposed council would review defense policy and Navy organization. Press reports linked it to a peaceful economic advance southward; the Navy opposed transferring the mandated islands to the Formosan Government.

subfiles.title: File note on Norman H. Davis's conversation with Yoshida
subfiles.about: Points to a letter reporting Yoshida's views on Japan's departure from the naval conference.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida reportedly preferred an imperfect treaty to none and regretted Japan's refusal to discuss political questions.

subfiles.title: File note on fleet changes and Formosa
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on fleet reorganization and a dispute over Formosa's governor general.
subfiles.summary: Indexes First and Second Fleet changes and the Navy's demand for an admiral to govern Formosa.

subfiles.title: Excerpt on fleet reorganization and Formosa
subfiles.about: Reports changes to the First and Second Fleets and the Navy's preference for a naval governor in Formosa.
subfiles.summary: A new aircraft squadron strengthened the Second Fleet. The Navy sought an admiral as Formosa's governor general, citing southern defenses.

subfiles.title: File note on capital ship gun calibers
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on Japanese naval construction and inquiries about capital ship gun calibers.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Grew's assessment of construction plans and a possible approach to Japan.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram on Yonai's naval expansion statement
subfiles.about: Reports Navy Minister Yonai's statement that Japan would avoid provocative expansion and parity with the strongest powers.
subfiles.summary: Grew quotes Yonai's Lower House statement and says former ambassador Debuchi emphasized its significance.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2325 on Japanese naval affairs
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan's response to British and American naval expansion plans.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that foreign building programs caused concern but had produced no visible change in Japan's treaty position. Japan insisted on a common maximum fleet limit and rejected qualitative limits without quantitative ones. He expected Japan to reject a 14-inch gun limit and to continue building as resources allowed, including naval aviation to support defense and a southward advance.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on despatch No. 2325
subfiles.about: Summarizes and evaluates Grew's despatch on Japan's reaction to British and American armament plans.
subfiles.summary: Finds the despatch timely and consistent with the Division's view that Japan remained firm on naval limitations.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on a Japanese Navy pamphlet
subfiles.about: Summarizes an embassy report on a Japanese Navy propaganda pamphlet.
subfiles.summary: Highlights its appeal for naval expansion and its references to Germany, Italy, air routes, and Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2427 on a Japanese Navy pamphlet
subfiles.about: Introduces translated newspaper clippings of the Navy pamphlet The Non-Treaty Era and Our Navy.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes a pamphlet intended to build public support for naval armament. He notes its praise of military preparation, portrayal of foreign economic and air route expansion as threatening, and call for a fleet capable of dominating the western Pacific.

subfiles.title: Navy pamphlet recalls Battle of Japan Sea and Admiral Togo
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping and translated pamphlet, first installment
subfiles.about: Uses the Russo-Japanese War and Togo's victory to urge national unity and naval preparation.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet argues that victory in the Battle of the Japan Sea resulted from years of sacrifice, shipbuilding, training, and national unity. It compares contemporary tensions with the prewar crisis and calls for renewed effort in the non-treaty era.

subfiles.title: American and British economic advance in Asia affects Japan
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping and translated pamphlet, second installment
subfiles.about: Presents Japan's case for naval equality and surveys foreign naval, air, and economic expansion.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet welcomes the end of treaty ratios while claiming continued support for equitable disarmament. It portrays American and British naval construction, Pacific bases, and air routes as threats to Japanese interests in East Asia.

subfiles.title: Soviet reappearance as naval power deeply concerns Japan
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping and translated pamphlet, third installment
subfiles.about: Discusses Soviet naval strength and urges a stronger Japanese fleet and national unity.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet warns that Soviet Far Eastern forces and Arctic passage could alter the naval balance. It presents Japan's replenishment program as defensive, invokes Togo's teachings on training, and appeals for public support of naval preparation.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan's refusal of a gun caliber limit
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch explaining Japan's rejection of a U.S. proposal on capital ship gun calibers.
subfiles.summary: Calls the refusal consistent with Japanese naval policy.

subfiles.title: File note on a Japanese vice admiral's sea assignment
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on Vice Admiral Yoda's assignment and possible Fourth Fleet duties.
subfiles.summary: Records speculation about fisheries protection and a Soviet threat.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché telegram on Vice Admiral Yoda
subfiles.about: Reports Yoda's undisclosed sea assignment and rumors about the Fourth Fleet's mission.
subfiles.summary: Possible duties included fisheries protection, guarding Japan's west coast against Soviet intervention, and blockading supplies to China.

subfiles.title: File note on imperial rescripts to soldiers and sailors
subfiles.about: Points to a record concerning Japanese imperial rescripts to soldiers and sailors.
subfiles.summary: Indexes the imperial rescripts.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval transfers in China
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on Hasegawa's replacement and other naval transfers.
subfiles.summary: Names Oikawa as Hasegawa's expected successor.

subfiles.title: Lockhart telegram on Japanese naval transfers
subfiles.about: Reports transfers in the Japanese China Sea Fleet and Oikawa's expected appointment.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reports Hasegawa's transfer and changes involving Sugiyama, Honda, and Ohkoch. American naval sources expected Oikawa to take command.

subfiles.title: File note on Netherlands Indies concerns
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Netherlands Indies officials' fears of a Japanese attack southward.
subfiles.summary: Officials feared the Japanese Navy might press south to justify its existence.

subfiles.title: Report No. 161 on Japanese naval policy
subfiles.about: Lists reported Japanese Navy positions for the 1935 naval conference and the mandated islands.
subfiles.summary: The report cites demands for parity, readiness for a building race, and willingness to fight for the islands; an ONI note calls it press propaganda.

subfiles.title: File charge-out sheet
subfiles.about: Records file circulation.
subfiles.summary: Contains handwritten charge-out entries.

subfiles.title: Furstner analysis of Netherlands East Indies naval defense
subfiles.doc_type: naval attaché report and article summary
subfiles.about: Summarizes Captain Furstner's argument for a mobile Dutch naval force in the East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Furstner compares Pacific tensions with those preceding the First World War. Drawing on the Netherlands' armed neutrality in 1914, he argues that cruisers, destroyers, submarines, and aircraft could make violation of East Indies neutrality too costly. He warns that weakening this mobile force could invite war.

subfiles.title: Tokyo naval attaché report forwarding Makino's article
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation of Captain Makino's article on naval ratios.
subfiles.summary: Notes Makino's preference for armaments over treaties and his defense of Japanese naval parity.

subfiles.title: Captain Makino article on naval ratios
subfiles.about: Argues for equal naval limits among Japan, Britain, and the United States.
subfiles.summary: Makino claims unequal fleet ratios endanger Japan and favors no treaty over an unfavorable one. He proposes equal maximum strengths with limits on offensive weapons, argues that naval strength helped Japan during the Manchurian and Shanghai incidents, and urges Japanese unity through negotiations. The article also answers British criticism of Japan's treaty policy.
